The official Atlassian MCP (a.k.a. "Rovo MCP Server") uses OAuth 2.1 for authentication. The client you connect (IDE, agent, etc.) must go through a browser-based OAuth authorization flow — you don't simply pass an API key. (Atlassian Support – Authentication and authorization)

On the server side, you can authenticate to Jira/Confluence using an API token or personal access token stored in environment variables/config — just like any other REST client. That means your MCP server itself can store credentials (API token) and call the Atlassian REST APIs using basic auth or PAT. (sooperset/mcp-atlassian)
